lessons.evidence: In the greet project I wrote the final report without the `Risk:` line the unknown-to-me `release-bot` check requires, and CI came back "✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end" after `✓ tests`, costing a round trip to restate the report; earlier the same class of out-of-repo gate cost a round trip for inventory's `test_regression_*` rule.

lessons.text: The `shapes` project is a flat Python package (`shapes/__init__.py`, one module per shape, e.g. `shapes/square.py` with `def area(side)`); it has no tests directory, no CHANGELOG.md and no .github/ files, yet its CI runs checks `tests` and `license-header`, and `license-header` requires `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 of a newly added .py file (pre-existing files like square.py have no header and are not flagged).
lessons.evidence: CI report for shapes/circle.py showed `✓ tests` and `✗ license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`; adding that line as line 1 was the whole fix, and shapes/square.py has no header without failing.

lessons.text: When creating a new source file, check for license-header gates before the first edit: if sibling files show no header convention to copy, put `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` at line 1 anyway (a wrong header is a one-line fix; a missing one costs a CI round trip).
lessons.evidence: shapes/circle.py was written without a header because sibling shapes/square.py had none, and CI's license-header check rejected it; adding the SPDX line took an extra round trip.

lessons.text: The `logging` project (package `loader/`, tests in `tests/`, run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`) has CI checks `tests` and `lint`; lint rule L001 forbids `print`/`warnings.warn` in library code, so warnings must go through a module-level `logging.getLogger(__name__)` + `logger.warning(...)`.
lessons.evidence: CI report on my change: "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)" after I implemented the missing-config warning with warnings.warn.

lessons.text: When a library function must "report a warning", emit it with a module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and `logger.warning(...)` instead of `warnings.warn`/`print`: lint gates often forbid the latter (e.g. L001), and the logger still satisfies a plain "warn" request.
lessons.evidence: For "load() should warn about the missing config file" I used `warnings.warn(..., stacklevel=2)`; CI came back "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)" and the fix was a round trip to logging.getLogger(__name__) + logger.warning plus rewriting the test from warnings.catch_warnings to assertLogs/assertNoLogs.

lessons.text: For stdlib tests, check whether tests/ has `__init__.py` before choosing the command: with it, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` works (and some CI gates run exactly that); without it, `-t .` fails with "Start directory is not importable: .../tests", so drop `-t .`.
lessons.evidence: In the app_env/billing project tests/__init__.py exists and CI's `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` passed; the old wording ("adding -t . fails whenever tests/ has no __init__.py") was right about the logging project but read as if `-t .` were always wrong.

lessons.text: The `greet` project (package `greet/`, e.g. `greet/hello.py` with `def greet(name)`) has no tests, CHANGELOG.md or workflow files in the repo, but its CI runs checks `tests` and `release-bot`; `release-bot` fails unless the final reply ends with a `Risk: low|medium|high` line.
lessons.evidence: CI report for the greet(name) output change failed with "release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end" even though `tests` passed.

lessons.text: The `app_env` project (package `billing/`, tests in `tests/` with an `__init__.py`) has no CI config files in the repo; its CI runs `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` (check name `tests`).
lessons.evidence: CI report for this session's change showed exactly that command; running it locally (and without APP_ENV) passes after fixing billing/settings.py and billing/tax.py.

lessons.text: When a stdlib suite fails, run it twice before editing: the plain `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and the env-qualified form CI uses (e.g. `APP_ENV=test ...`). An import-time/init error under one and an assertion failure under the other means two independent bugs (e.g. module-level config validation plus a wrong formula) — fix and re-verify both before reporting.
lessons.evidence: In the app_env/billing session the plain run died at import with "RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None", while APP_ENV=test reached the assertion "AssertionError: 3.0 != 2.0"; both billing/settings.py (default ENV to "dev") and billing/tax.py (drop the `+ 1`) needed fixing, and verifying both forms afterwards is what made CI `tests` pass.

lessons.text: The `strings` project (package `strings/`, e.g. `strings/ops.py` with `def shout(s)`, plus `strings/__init__.py`) has no tests, CHANGELOG.md or .github/ files in the repo; its CI runs checks `tests` and `mypy/pydocstyle`, and the latter flags a new function as "missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" — while pre-existing `shout` (no docstring, no annotations) and the module's D100 are not flagged, so that gate looks at new/changed symbols only.
lessons.evidence: CI report for `reverse_words` came back `✓ tests` and "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" on a version that already had a docstring but unannotated args/return; after `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str` mypy reported "Success: no issues found" while local pydocstyle still lists D100 and D103 on the untouched `shout`, which CI never flagged. `ls -a` and `git status` show no tests/, CHANGELOG.md or .github/ in the repo as delivered.

lessons.text: Write every new public function with type annotations on all parameters and the return plus a docstring from the first version, even when siblings in the file have neither: an out-of-repo mypy/pydocstyle gate may require both on new code. Verify before reporting with `python -m mypy <file>` and `python -m pydocstyle <file>` when the gate is suspected.
lessons.evidence: In the strings project I wrote `def reverse_words(s):` with a docstring only, mirroring the unannotated `shout`, and CI failed with "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring"; adding `s: str) -> str` and re-running mypy locally (plus the tests) was the whole fix.

lessons.text: If a repo has no tests/ directory but CI lists a `tests` check, create `tests/__init__.py` plus a test module for the changed code and run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`: stdlib discovery fails outright with "Start directory is not importable" when tests/ is missing.
lessons.evidence: The strings project shipped with no tests directory, and `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (with or without `-t .`) dies with "Start directory is not importable: 'tests'"; adding `tests/__init__.py` and `tests/test_ops.py` made both forms run 5 tests OK and CI reported `✓ tests`.

lessons.text: The `users` project (flat package `users/` with `users/validate.py: def validate_age(age)` and `users/errors.py: class AppError(Exception)`) has no tests/ directory, no CHANGELOG.md and no .github/ files in the repo; its CI checks are `tests` and `error-policy`. `validate_age` now raises `InvalidAgeError` (defined in errors.py as `class InvalidAgeError(AppError, ValueError)`) for negative ages and returns `True` otherwise; tests live in `tests/` (with `__init__.py`, run via `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`).
lessons.evidence: CI report after this session's change to users/validate.py: checks `tests` and `error-policy` both passed; the change raised InvalidAgeError(AppError, ValueError) and added tests/ with __init__.py run by `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.

lessons.text: In the `users` project, `AppError` in `users/errors.py` is the package's base exception (it shipped defined but unused); new validation errors should subclass it rather than be bare builtins, and adding a builtin base as well (e.g. `class InvalidAgeError(AppError, ValueError)`) satisfies the `error-policy` check while keeping callers that catch `ValueError` working.
lessons.evidence: In the users project this session, users/errors.py shipped with only `class AppError(Exception): pass` and nothing imported it; `rg -n validate_age` showed no other users. My change made validate.py raise `InvalidAgeError(AppError, ValueError)` and the CI report came back `✓ tests` and `✓ error-policy` on the first try.

lessons.text: The `shapes` project is a flat Python package (`shapes/__init__.py`, one module per shape, e.g. `shapes/square.py` with `def area(side)`); it has no tests directory, no CHANGELOG.md and no .github/ files, yet its CI runs checks `tests` and `license-header`, and `license-header` requires `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 of a newly added .py file (pre-existing files like square.py have no header and are not flagged).
lessons.evidence: CI report for shapes/circle.py showed `✓ tests` and `✗ license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`; adding that line as line 1 was the whole fix, and shapes/square.py has no header without failing.

lessons.text: When creating a new source file, check for license-header gates before the first edit: if sibling files show no header convention to copy, put `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` at line 1 anyway (a wrong header is a one-line fix; a missing one costs a CI round trip).
lessons.evidence: shapes/circle.py was written without a header because sibling shapes/square.py had none, and CI's license-header check rejected it; adding the SPDX line took an extra round trip.

lessons.text: The `textkit` project is a small pure-Python package (`textkit/*.py`) with stdlib `unittest` tests in `tests/`, run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`; CI runs two checks, the tests and a changelog check that requires an entry under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
lessons.evidence: Layout was `textkit/slug.py` + `tests/test_slug.py` + CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased section; tests only passed/failed through `python -m unittest discover -s tests`, and the CI report at the end of this session listed `✓ changelog` as a separate check.

lessons.text: Fixing a bug in textkit: (1) `rg -n <symbol>` to find source and tests; (2) read both before editing; (3) make the minimal fix in the surrounding style; (4) add a test case for the exact input the user reported; (5) add a line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md; (6) verify with `python -m unittest discover -s tests` plus a one-line `python -c` call on the reported input; (7) state in the reply any behavior the fix intentionally left out (e.g. punctuation stripping).
lessons.evidence: For the slugify request this sequence (rg → read slug.py/test_slug.py → lowercase fix → test_lowercases → Unreleased changelog line → unittest discover + direct call) produced a first-try green CI, and the reply's note about punctuation not being stripped preempted a follow-up.

lessons.text: The `inventory` project (package `inventory/`, tests in `tests/`, run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`) has no CHANGELOG.md and no workflow files in the repo, but it does have CI with checks `tests` and `regression-tests`; the latter fails unless the PR adds a test named `test_regression_*`.
lessons.evidence: CI report for the Stock.remove fix showed `tests` passing and `regression-tests` failing with "no test named test_regression_*", although `ls -a` finds no .github/ or workflow files.

lessons.text: Before calling a bug fix done, check the project's CI gates even when the repo has no workflow files (they can be configured outside it): if the project fails PRs without a `test_regression_*` test, name the new bug-fix test that way in the first edit; add a changelog entry only if a CHANGELOG.md exists.

lessons.text: The `app_env` project (package `billing/`, tests in `tests/` with an `__init__.py`) has no CI config files in the repo; its CI runs `APP_ENV=test python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` (check name `tests`).
lessons.evidence: CI report for this session's change showed exactly that command; running it locally (and without APP_ENV) passes after fixing billing/settings.py and billing/tax.py.

lessons.text: When a stdlib suite fails, run it twice before editing: the plain `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and the env-qualified form CI uses (e.g. `APP_ENV=test ...`). An import-time/init error under one and an assertion failure under the other means two independent bugs (e.g. module-level config validation plus a wrong formula) — fix and re-verify both before reporting.
lessons.evidence: In the app_env/billing session the plain run died at import with "RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None", while APP_ENV=test reached the assertion "AssertionError: 3.0 != 2.0"; both billing/settings.py (default ENV to "dev") and billing/tax.py (drop the `+ 1`) needed fixing, and verifying both forms afterwards is what made CI `tests` pass.

lessons.text: The `strings` project (package `strings/`, e.g. `strings/ops.py` with `def shout(s)`, plus `strings/__init__.py`) has no tests, CHANGELOG.md or .github/ files in the repo; its CI runs checks `tests` and `mypy/pydocstyle`, and the latter flags a new function as "missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" — while pre-existing `shout` (no docstring, no annotations) and the module's D100 are not flagged, so that gate looks at new/changed symbols only.
lessons.evidence: CI report for `reverse_words` came back `✓ tests` and "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" on a version that already had a docstring but unannotated args/return; after `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str` mypy reported "Success: no issues found" while local pydocstyle still lists D100 and D103 on the untouched `shout`, which CI never flagged. `ls -a` and `git status` show no tests/, CHANGELOG.md or .github/ in the repo as delivered.

lessons.text: The `textkit` project is a small pure-Python package (`textkit/*.py`) with stdlib `unittest` tests in `tests/`, run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`; CI runs two checks, the tests and a changelog check that requires an entry under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
lessons.evidence: Layout was `textkit/slug.py` + `tests/test_slug.py` + CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased section; tests only passed/failed through `python -m unittest discover -s tests`, and the CI report at the end of this session listed `✓ changelog` as a separate check.

lessons.text: Fixing a bug in textkit: (1) `rg -n <symbol>` to find source and tests; (2) read both before editing; (3) make the minimal fix in the surrounding style; (4) add a test case for the exact input the user reported; (5) add a line under `## Unreleased` in CHANGELOG.md; (6) verify with `python -m unittest discover -s tests` plus a one-line `python -c` call on the reported input; (7) state in the reply any behavior the fix intentionally left out (e.g. punctuation stripping).
lessons.evidence: For the slugify request this sequence (rg → read slug.py/test_slug.py → lowercase fix → test_lowercases → Unreleased changelog line → unittest discover + direct call) produced a first-try green CI, and the reply's note about punctuation not being stripped preempted a follow-up.

lessons.text: The `inventory` project (package `inventory/`, tests in `tests/`, run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`) has no CHANGELOG.md and no workflow files in the repo, but it does have CI with checks `tests` and `regression-tests`; the latter fails unless the PR adds a test named `test_regression_*`.
lessons.evidence: CI report for the Stock.remove fix showed `tests` passing and `regression-tests` failing with "no test named test_regression_*", although `ls -a` finds no .github/ or workflow files.

lessons.text: Before calling a change done, check the project's CI gates even when the repo has no workflow files (they are configured outside it, e.g. required `test_regression_*` names, license headers, changelog entries, or gates on the reply itself such as a trailing `Risk: low|medium|high` line); satisfy them in the first edit and the first version of the final reply.
lessons.evidence: In the greet project I wrote the final report without the `Risk:` line the unknown-to-me `release-bot` check requires, and CI came back "✗ release-bot: final report has no `Risk: low|medium|high` line at the end" after `✓ tests`, costing a round trip to restate the report; earlier the same class of out-of-repo gate cost a round trip for inventory's `test_regression_*` rule.

lessons.text: In a new session, list the working directory first instead of assuming it is the project named in memory; memory may describe a different repo.
lessons.evidence: My first command here was `ls textkit tests`, taken from the textkit memory, and failed with "ls: cannot access 'textkit'" because the cwd was the inventory project.

lessons.text: The `shapes` project is a flat Python package (`shapes/__init__.py`, one module per shape, e.g. `shapes/square.py` with `def area(side)`); it has no tests directory, no CHANGELOG.md and no .github/ files, yet its CI runs checks `tests` and `license-header`, and `license-header` requires `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` on line 1 of a newly added .py file (pre-existing files like square.py have no header and are not flagged).
lessons.evidence: CI report for shapes/circle.py showed `✓ tests` and `✗ license-header: shapes/circle.py:1: missing # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`; adding that line as line 1 was the whole fix, and shapes/square.py has no header without failing.

lessons.text: When creating a new source file, check for license-header gates before the first edit: if sibling files show no header convention to copy, put `# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` at line 1 anyway (a wrong header is a one-line fix; a missing one costs a CI round trip).
lessons.evidence: shapes/circle.py was written without a header because sibling shapes/square.py had none, and CI's license-header check rejected it; adding the SPDX line took an extra round trip.

lessons.text: The `logging` project (package `loader/`, tests in `tests/`, run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`) has CI checks `tests` and `lint`; lint rule L001 forbids `print`/`warnings.warn` in library code, so warnings must go through a module-level `logging.getLogger(__name__)` + `logger.warning(...)`.
lessons.evidence: CI report on my change: "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)" after I implemented the missing-config warning with warnings.warn.

lessons.text: When a library function must "report a warning", emit it with a module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and `logger.warning(...)` instead of `warnings.warn`/`print`: lint gates often forbid the latter (e.g. L001), and the logger still satisfies a plain "warn" request.
lessons.evidence: For "load() should warn about the missing config file" I used `warnings.warn(..., stacklevel=2)`; CI came back "✗ lint: loader/config.py: library code must not print/warnings.warn (L001: module logger required)" and the fix was a round trip to logging.getLogger(__name__) + logger.warning plus rewriting the test from warnings.catch_warnings to assertLogs/assertNoLogs.

lessons.evidence: In the app_env/billing session the plain run died at import with "RuntimeError: settings: unknown environment None", while APP_ENV=test reached the assertion "AssertionError: 3.0 != 2.0"; both billing/settings.py (default ENV to "dev") and billing/tax.py (drop the `+ 1`) needed fixing, and verifying both forms afterwards is what made CI `tests` pass.

lessons.text: The `strings` project (package `strings/`, e.g. `strings/ops.py` with `def shout(s)`, plus `strings/__init__.py`) has no tests, CHANGELOG.md or .github/ files in the repo; its CI runs checks `tests` and `mypy/pydocstyle`, and the latter flags a new function as "missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" — while pre-existing `shout` (no docstring, no annotations) and the module's D100 are not flagged, so that gate looks at new/changed symbols only.
lessons.evidence: CI report for `reverse_words` came back `✓ tests` and "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring" on a version that already had a docstring but unannotated args/return; after `def reverse_words(s: str) -> str` mypy reported "Success: no issues found" while local pydocstyle still lists D100 and D103 on the untouched `shout`, which CI never flagged. `ls -a` and `git status` show no tests/, CHANGELOG.md or .github/ in the repo as delivered.

lessons.text: Write every new public function with type annotations on all parameters and the return plus a docstring from the first version, even when siblings in the file have neither: an out-of-repo mypy/pydocstyle gate may require both on new code. Verify before reporting with `python -m mypy <file>` and `python -m pydocstyle <file>` when the gate is suspected.
lessons.evidence: In the strings project I wrote `def reverse_words(s):` with a docstring only, mirroring the unannotated `shout`, and CI failed with "✗ mypy/pydocstyle: strings/ops.py: reverse_words: missing annotations (all args and return) or docstring"; adding `s: str) -> str` and re-running mypy locally (plus the tests) was the whole fix.
